T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: No study measures household poverty against a comparison; the outcome is reached through yields, catch and appraisals, most of them projections, grey literature or reports by implementers [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1, ev_frmg_erw09_1, ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. The Viet Nam shellfish-yield finding now sits in the food row, since it measures harvest rather than income. One source finds harm: a Bangladesh appraisal projects that most mangrove-and-shrimp systems lose money for landowners in the early years, and two stay below break-even for longer [ev_economic_return_rahman18_4, ev_economic_return_rahman18_5]. Several results are held out because their value goes to society rather than households: a World Bank project in Viet Nam returned only 3.6 percent without counting carbon, giving a negative net value [ev_economic_return_wbicr6719_3]; a Senegal model gives benefit-cost ratios of 2.27 to 5.71 mostly from avoided damage [ev_economic_return_iisd26_7]; and in Indonesia restoration pays in most districts but not where land is valuable, such as Eastern Sumatra and Kalimantan [ev_economic_return_wbidn22_3]. Mangrove planting is also cheaper than breakwaters, but that saving goes to the public [ev_frmg_nara16_3, ev_frmg_nara16_4]. The Gujarat result is household recall with no comparison villages, from grey literature [ev_household_income_becklange16_1], and the Philippine benefits are borrowed from a Thai valuation rather than measured [ev_economic_return_ferrer11_1]. A global model giving benefit-cost ratios between 3 and 6 for restoring mangroves in front of dikes is held out, because its benefit is avoided flood damage to buildings, which goes to society [ev_economic_return_tiggeloven26_2]. A Caribbean model finding that flood-protection benefits outweigh restoration costs along 181 coastal units in 20 countries and territories is held out for the same reason [ev_economic_return_beck22_1].
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: Mangrove restoration moderately reduces rural poverty, reaching household incomes mainly through fish, crabs and shellfish. In a rehabilitated basin in Java a new finfish fishery earns fishers about 1.05 USD per hour [ev_household_income_debrot22_2], and a Philippine survey suggests replanted mangroves add USD 564–2316/ha/y to local incomes [ev_household_income_debrot22_3]. Appraisals of the planting itself are mostly positive: a global meta-analysis finds benefits outweigh costs [ev_economic_return_su21_1], commune benefit-cost ratios in Viet Nam range from 3.06 to 68.92 [ev_economic_return_ifrc11_1], and Mexican pilot sites had positive net present values [ev_frmg_mxicr_1]. A Senegal model assumes women's income from oyster gathering rises by 10% [ev_household_income_iisd26_4]. In Gujarat, India, 34 of 227 households surveyed reported higher fishing income after mangrove planting [ev_household_income_becklange16_1], and in the Philippines a costing of letting disused fishponds revert to mangrove gives benefit-cost ratios of 4.53 to 4.69 [ev_economic_return_ferrer11_1].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: Results depend on where and how mangroves are planted. In parts of Bac Lieu the replanted mangroves washed away and the coast kept eroding fast [ev_frmg_vnppar_2], and in Indonesia mangroves planted on pond dykes and inside ponds did not protect the coast: after spring tides and storms the trees stood but most dykes were destroyed [ev_erosion_hazard_bosma20_1]. The Vietnam figures are uncontrolled project monitoring and visual checks [ev_frmg_vnppar_1, ev_frmg_vnppar_2], the Bangladesh evidence is a practitioner rating and a project claim [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4300_2019_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_ahammad13_2], and the Indonesian dam results come from authors linked to the implementing organisations [ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_1, ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_5]. There is no controlled measurement of erosion under mangrove restoration. The Bangladesh account is a summary in grey literature, and much of it is planting on newly formed land rather than restoring lost mangrove [ev_sediment_retention_becklange16_1]. The Vietnam fringe observations describe shoreline building with no size given [ev_sediment_retention_fagh17_5]. Only a few units give a size, which holds the rating at moderate.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: Mangroves slow water and trap sediment, so the coast builds up instead of washing away. In Vietnam's southern Mekong Delta, project monitoring reports coastal erosion reduced by 40 percent in Ca Mau because of replanted mangroves [ev_frmg_vnppar_1], and evaluators found mangroves had turned the Soc Trang coast into an area that builds up [ev_frmg_vnppar_2]. In Bangladesh practitioners report less surface runoff under the plantation canopy [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4300_2019_surface_runoff], and project staff report better land stabilisation [ev_erosion_hazard_ahammad13_2]. In Indonesia, permeable brushwood dams that let mangroves return trapped about 0.5 m of sediment in four months while the coast kept eroding elsewhere [ev_sediment_retention_winterwerp20_1]. In Bangladesh, government mangrove planting on coastal mudflats is reported to have been very effective in building land, with rapid sediment build-up [ev_sediment_retention_becklange16_1]. Detailed observations of a fringe mangrove forest in Vietnam, part of it planted, found the mangroves engineer the landscape, favouring sediment deposition and dissipating waves [ev_sediment_retention_fagh17_5].

justification.mechanism: The evidence points to a small reduction in flood impact, with no size given. Wooded riparian strips act on the water pathway rather than on the crop: they slow the flow of water from the land into receiving water bodies by increasing infiltration, reducing flow velocity and providing temporary storage [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_1], and mature woodland is the more effective form because of its structural complexity and the deadwood it delivers to the watercourse [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_2]. The only field finding runs from removal: in Marqués de Comillas, Chiapas, floods along with the seasonal drying of permanent streams and altered river dynamics were associated with the loss of riparian forest [ev_flood_hazard_meli19_4]. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses rates the chance of reducing recurring floods as high or very high in about 1/7 to 1/5 of the landscapes where buffers are set up [ev_flood_hazard_englund21_8].

The implied mechanism is retention and conveyance of flood water in a vegetated headwater floodplain.

Zone 2 is a managed strip of trees or shrubs extending another 18.3 m (minimum width) upland, beyond zone 1. This zone is managed for nutrient removal to stimulate efficacy of nutrient uptake. T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: The direction is consistent but, apart from one model, nothing here measures how much biodiversity is gained: the quantities reported are buffer widths and thresholds of vegetation loss, not effect sizes, so the row states a direction rather than a size. Width is the live condition — below the widths cited above the same reviews record composition change instead of gain — and several outcomes did not move at all: small-mammal abundance did not differ among buffers of 20, 40 and 60 m, nor between riparian strips of 20-200 m and controls up to four years after their creation [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_8, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_9]; plant species richness was similar in unbuffered field margins, narrow and wide buffers, with only flower abundance higher in the wide ones [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_2]; evidence on buffers' effectiveness at increasing botanical diversity is conflicting [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_1]; fish decline thresholds did not differ significantly between buffer sizes and invertebrate thresholds did not differ between biomes [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_7, ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_9]; and investigations of past riparian restoration projects in the southwestern United States found highly variable recovery of desirable plant communities, including frequent failure of planted species to establish [ev_biodiversity_outcome_gonzalez15_1]. Two findings are measured harm rather than a missing gain: overtaxing the nutrient-removal capacity of riparian zones and floodplain wetlands may lead to losses of biodiversity and production of nitrous oxides [ev_biodiversity_outcome_maye07_4], and in urban North Carolina stream restorations the increased temperature and light that stimulate early nutrient uptake had severe consequences for instream biota and shifted the stream toward autotrophy and algal biomass — in projects that bundle channel engineering with riparian replanting and state no share for either [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mcmi14_1]. Where a buffer is compared with intact forest rather than with an unbuffered stream, a shortfall is not harm: higher total avian abundance in buffer strips than in forested streamside controls was attributed to edge and clearcut-tolerant species, a change in composition [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_6]. Much of the width evidence comes from strips left standing after harvesting in forestry [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_7]: it shows what retaining riparian vegetation does at harvest, not what establishing a strip on cleared farmland would deliver, and the revegetation finding for trout is the closest this row comes to the latter [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_2]. Finally the whole base sits in temperate and boreal forestry and farming landscapes in Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Great Britain, Mexico and the United States, and the Belgian gains are model results; nothing here was measured in a low- or lower-middle-income setting, and the Brazilian thresholds are the closest available analogue.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: A buffer keeps, or puts back, a strip of woody vegetation between the field or the cut-block and the channel, and biodiversity responds through the habitat held in that strip and through the water it filters. Width governs the habitat side: streams with buffers of 30 m or more showed no impact of harvest on invertebrates, while narrower strips changed species diversity in proportion to their width [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_1]; bird assemblages needed more, with 150 and 175 m argued as the widths that would maintain 90 and 95% of preharvest species, and more than 50 m to hold bird densities and prevent changes to community structure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_3, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_4]; moose densities were greater in 60 m strips left after harvesting than in blocks that retained no buffer [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_7]; and trout populations recovered once revegetation by shrubs and trees brought down the stream temperature that had followed harvesting to the margin [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_2]. The water side works through what the strip stops: buffers reduce sediments and contaminants entering the watercourse, improving the ecological status of waterbodies and favouring pollution-sensitive mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies over pollutant-tolerant chironomids [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_4]. The Brazilian evidence measures the same relationship from the losing end, and it is the sharpest statement of how little vegetation can be given up: aquatic invertebrate bioindicators declined abruptly after a mean loss of 6.5% of the riparian vegetation within 50 m of the stream, and only 2.9% in the Amazon biome [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_4, ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_5], with thresholds lowest in the narrowest buffers, so vegetation close to the water is what carries the effect [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_6]. At landscape scale the buffer is also a corridor: conserving and restoring riparian buffers is credited with enhancing connectivity in fragmented landscapes and letting native species persist in habitat remnants [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_2], and on the Ayuquila the longitudinal continuity of the riverbanks increased and physical habitat quality improved after restoration [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_6]. A model of riparian forest along a river in Belgium finds that the best options raise an index of pollution-sensitive stream insects by up to 96.0%, while the diversity of diatoms (tiny algae) changes little, by up to 5.2% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_witing22_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_witing22_3].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: Apart from the Belgian model, which is a model result from a rich country [ev_biodiversity_outcome_witing22_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_witing22_3], most of the quantity in this row is loss-framed: the Brazilian thresholds measure what clearing costs, not what a restored strip returns, and regrowth is not guaranteed to run the film backwards. Within that dataset, fish thresholds did not differ significantly between buffer sizes [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_7] and invertebrate and EPTOD thresholds did not differ between biomes [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_9]. For vegetation the signal is weak or absent: evidence on the effectiveness of buffers at increasing botanical diversity is conflicting [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_1], and plant species richness was similar in unbuffered field margins, narrow buffers and wide ones, only flower abundance being greater in the wide ones [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_2]. Width and subsequent management can undo the effect — selective logging changed moss communities in 15 m buffers though not in 30 m ones [ev_biodiversity_outcome_olde19_5]. The Mexican and Latin American claims are hedged review statements and a case-study observation of habitat quality rather than biodiversity measurement [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_6], and the fish-recovery finding is a forestry case reported second-hand in a review [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_2]. The pool is boreal, temperate and Neotropical upper-middle-income; nothing is measured in a low-income farming landscape.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: Where riparian vegetation is allowed back, the gains reported are habitat continuity and water quality rather than counts of species planted. Fish populations recovered after stream temperatures fell following revegetation by shrubs and trees, having dropped four-fold where harvest reached the stream margin and summer temperature peaked at 30 degrees [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_2]. Buffers reduce the sediments and contaminants entering the watercourse, improving the ecological status of waterbodies and favouring pollution-sensitive mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies over tolerant chironomids [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_4]. On the Ayuquila, longitudinal continuity of the riverbanks increased and physical habitat quality improved after restoration [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_6], and conserving and restoring buffers is argued to enhance connectivity in fragmented landscapes and let native species persist in habitat remnants [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_2]. T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: Read the positive findings against what they were compared with. The higher avian abundance was attributed to edge and clearcut tolerant species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_6], which is a shift in composition, and where the comparator was undisturbed lakeshore forest rather than unbuffered harvest, bird density and species richness were lower in the buffer strip [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_5]. Small mammals did not respond at all, either among buffers of 20, 40 and 60 m or between 20-200 m strips and controls up to four years after their creation [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_8, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_9]. Establishment is a real failure mode for this family: investigations of past riparian restoration projects in the southwestern US found a very high degree of variability in the recovery of desirable plant communities, including frequent failure of planted species to establish [ev_biodiversity_outcome_gonzalez15_1]. Two further findings are of measured harm — overtaxing the nutrient removal capacity of riparian zones may lead to losses of biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_maye07_4], and in newly restored reaches the increased temperature and light have severe consequences for instream biota and shift the stream toward autotrophy and algal biomass [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mcmi14_1], the latter from urban stream restoration bundled with channel regrading and in-channel structures. Note also what the sources actually are: every positive finding is a forestry retention buffer left standing after timber harvest, reported second-hand in a buffer-width review, not a buffer planted on farmland, and all of it is temperate or boreal North America at high income.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: The gains reported here come from a strip of woody vegetation held between the harvested or cropped land and the stream. Streams with buffers of 30 m or more showed no impact of harvest on invertebrates, while below that width species diversity changed in proportion to buffer width [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_1]. Birds need more width than invertebrates: 150 and 175 m were argued to maintain 90 and 95% of preharvest species along mid-order streams [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_3], and more than 50 m to maintain bird densities and prevent changes to community structure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_4]; total avian abundance was higher in buffer strips than in forested streamside controls [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_6], and moose densities were greater in 60 m strips than in blocks that retained none [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_7].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: These quantities are not comparable with each other and none is a transferable per-hectare figure. The UK value is an estimate taken from secondary sources and is printed as an annual rate for what the same sentence calls a capacity to store [ev_carbon_sequestration_cole20_1] — so it is indicative only. The Quebec measurement spreads from 52 down to 6.4 t per hectare between sites of the same planting [ev_carbon_sequestration_fort10_1], so site fertility, not the practice, dominates the outcome; it is also aboveground stock in a young stand, with no soil carbon measured. The Costa Rican 1.4% is a modelled scenario output rather than a measurement, from a study whose authors flag their sediment model as over-estimating erosion on steep ground and their nutrient model as very sensitive to its retention parameter [ev_carbon_sequestration_lang22_1]. The European soil-carbon finding is a model and gives no figure [ev_soil_organic_carbon_englund21_7]. Nothing in this row is measured in a low- or lower-middle-income landscape: Canada, the UK, Costa Rica and the European study area are all classified high-income, and the evidence is temperate apart from the Costa Rican model.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: The evidence points to a small gain in carbon. The carbon is in the woody biomass the buffer grows, above and below ground: a UK review puts the storage capacity of wooded buffers at an estimated 80 t per hectare per year across both pools [ev_carbon_sequestration_cole20_1]. Measured in planted hybrid poplar buffers on southern Quebec farm streams, carbon in total aboveground biomass reached 52 t per hectare at the most fertile site and as little as 6.4 t per hectare at the least [ev_carbon_sequestration_fort10_1], and aboveground biomass and carbon in the poplars were statistically higher than in the poplar understorey and in the adjacent unmanaged herbaceous buffer [ev_carbon_sequestration_fort10_2] — planting trees, not simply fencing the strip, is what moved the stock. Scaled by model, bringing riparian forest up to the minimum that Costa Rican Forest Law 7575 requires raises the national carbon stock by 1.4%, or 7.0 Mt [ev_carbon_sequestration_lang22_1]. A European model of buffer strips planted on cropland finds the gain in soil carbon substantial in absolute terms, but unlikely to make up much of the soil carbon already lost across Europe [ev_soil_organic_carbon_englund21_7].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: Nothing here is a measured reduction in flood damage to a farm. The Chiapas finding describes what losing riparian forest was associated with, in a case study, not what establishing a buffer delivers [ev_flood_hazard_meli19_4]. The European estimate is a model, and in most landscapes it does not rate the flood benefit as high [ev_flood_hazard_englund21_8]. The review that states the benefit confines it to moderate flooding and makes it depend on the extent, location, age and density of the woodland, with mature woodland more effective [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_2], which a new strip is not. No source reports a buffer holding up in a severe or extreme flood. The effect works on water moving into streams and rivers, so the farm giving up land need not be where the benefit lands. The sources are a UK review and a European model, both from rich, temperate countries, plus one upper-middle-income case from Mexico; there is no low-income evidence.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: The evidence points to a small reduction in flood impact, with no size given. As a hazard-facing outcome, the buffer works on conveyance rather than on the asset: wooded buffers contribute to natural flood management, slowing the flow of water from the land into receiving water bodies by increasing infiltration, reducing flow velocity and providing temporary water storage [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_1], with mature woodland the more effective form because of its structural complexity and the deadwood it adds to watercourses [ev_flood_hazard_cole20_2]. The counterpart evidence is from removal: in Chiapas, floods, seasonal stream drying and altered river dynamics were associated with riparian forest loss [ev_flood_hazard_meli19_4]. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses rates the chance of reducing recurring floods as high or very high in about 1/7 to 1/5 of the landscapes where buffers are set up [ev_flood_hazard_englund21_8].

T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: The evidence points to a small reduction in flood impact, with no size given. T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: What the evidence shows is that keeping a wide, unthinned strip of mature forest beside a clear-cut holds the streamside microclimate closer to unlogged forest than a narrow or thinned strip does; the direction comes from the failures of the narrow and thinned strips, read the other way round. It does not show that establishing a buffer on cleared or farmed land cools anything, and it does not measure heat stress on crops, livestock or people: the outcome is the riparian forest's own air temperature, humidity and canopy openness. Even the best-performing strip did not fully hold air humidity [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_3]. A single boreal, high-income study; no tropical or low-income evidence.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: This is retention evidence: strips of the existing mature spruce riparian forest left standing between a clear-cut and the stream in boreal Finland, measured against unlogged control streamsides. Width and thinning decided whether the strip held its microclimate. 15-meter strips with or without selective logging, and 30-meter strips with selective logging, were insufficient in maintaining temperature, relative humidity and canopy openness at control levels [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_1]; 30-meter strips without selective logging differed only little from controls, although they had significantly lower mean air humidity [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_2, ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_3]; and at 10 m from the stream every buffer except the unlogged 30-meter ones had significantly higher canopy openness than controls [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_4].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: What the buffer traps depends on what the soil is made of: the same plots retained 93% of sand and silt but only 52% of clay [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3], and a 4 m grass buffer on a 2% slope was almost 100% effective on sandy loams but only 35% effective on silty clay loams [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2]. Width buys less than it appears to: retention rises sharply over the first 10 m and then tails off [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], widening from 50 m to 100 m added only 4.6% and 4.0% in the two models tested [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2], and 30 m buffers were unable to prevent increases in stream sedimentation after partial clearcutting [ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Most of the large percentages come from plot-scale experiments under simulated rainfall or pumped runoff rather than field-scale monitoring [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1], and the mass reductions are achieved partly because water infiltrates and is lost, which is not the same as a cleaner stream [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. Two of the strongest-looking numbers are modelled rather than measured — the 30.5 and 36.2% retention gains from widening Prince Edward Island buffers [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1] and the Costa Rican 3.9% [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1] — and the Brazilian values are correlations across a handful of watersheds, not experiments [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2]. Two of the bank findings are farmer perception and cited background rather than measurement [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. The two Dosskey-reviewed findings above are themselves citations of other studies, not new measurement by Dosskey et al. [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_5, ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. The measured core is narrow in origin: repeated studies on one Iowa stream, Bear Creek, supply a large share of the runoff and sediment figures [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], alongside Kansas, Missouri and Connecticut plots; apart from China and Brazil the whole pool is temperate high-income, and no measurement comes from a low-income farming system. The European figures are model results from rich countries [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: The rating is a small reduction in erosion risk. Most of the large percentages below measure runoff and soil caught in the strip at the stream edge; the one estimate of soil loss avoided on the cropland itself is small. The buffer intercepts overland flow before it reaches the channel: dense switchgrass stops concentrated flow from the field and allows infiltration rates well above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], which cut runoff by 58.3% behind a 7 m switchgrass buffer and 81.5% behind the wider switchgrass-woody buffer over 19 natural events [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6], and by more than 77% in Kansas grass-shrub plots [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. What the water no longer carries is trapped: 70% of incoming sediment behind the grass buffer and more than 92% behind the grass-woody buffer under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3] with trapping never falling below 71% in any storm [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 97% behind an 8 m grass strip and 91% within the first 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3], and 92% for woody, 72% for grass and 50% for shrub strips in the Guishui catchment against a bare control that trapped 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]. Trapping efficiency rises sharply over the first 10 m and then tails off [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], and narrow strips are already effective [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]; in Brazilian third-order watersheds, suspended and organic solids fall as riparian forest cover rises [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], and a national model adds 3.9% to sediment retention [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1]. A US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass cut sediment concentration in overland flow by 92% [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_5], and McKergow et al. (2003) found that vegetation restoration of denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced catchment sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly by reducing bank erosion and stabilising the stream channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. The second pathway is the bank itself: planting trees stabilises river banks, reducing erosion and sediment loss [ev_streambank_erosion_cole20_1, ev_streambank_erosion_osbo93_17], willow posts held further collapse to an additional 0.3 m of bank through the 1993 floods and streambank integrity was maintained on the planted reach [ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2], farmers on the Ayuquila identify tree roots as what avoids riverbank erosion during floods [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5], and replacing riparian forest with other land cover brings bank erosion [ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they avoid 6.3% of the soil lost to water erosion on cropland in the landscapes where they are set up (1.2% across the EU and UK), and separately catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on European cropland [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: Only the Chinese result is a measured contrast, and it shows how far the effect can fall: a shrub strip trapped 50% where woody vegetation trapped 92%, and the bare control already trapped 22% on its own, so the attributable gain is smaller than the headline [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]; those strips were also long-established rather than newly planted. The Brazilian numbers are correlation coefficients across a small set of watersheds, not experiments, and cannot be read as effect sizes [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2]. The rest of the row is cited background or an uncited introductory assertion [ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11] and a farmer perception recorded in a case study [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5]. Nothing here reports performance in an extreme storm, in a low-income system, or over time as the trapped sediment accumulates.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: In the upper-middle-income evidence the effect is trapping in the vegetated strip and holding of the bank. Along the Guishui River, buffer strips reduced average outflow sediment by 92% where the vegetation was woody, 72% where it was grasses and 50% where it was shrubs, against a bare control whose own trapping efficiency was 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3] — vegetation type, not merely the presence of a strip, sets the size of the effect. In Brazilian third-order watersheds, suspended and organic solids in the stream fall as riparian-zone forest cover rises [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], consistent with buffers of proper design trapping sediment from the runoff passing through [ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1]. On the bank, replacing riparian forest with other land cover leads to bank erosion [ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11], and farmers on the Ayuquila identify the role of tree roots in avoiding riverbank erosion during flood events [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: The strong figures are for coarse material: the same buffers retained 93% of sand and silt but only 52% of clay [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3], so the fraction that carries phosphorus and travels furthest is the fraction least trapped. Extra width pays little — widening from 50 m to 100 m added only 4.6 and 4.0% in the two models [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2] — and those widening figures are modelled rather than measured, from a study whose authors note the models do not place the widened buffer at the field edge [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. The percentages themselves come mostly from plot-scale work under simulated rainfall or pumped runoff [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], where mass reductions partly reflect water infiltrating rather than a cleaner stream [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. A large share of the quantified evidence is a single Iowa stream, Bear Creek, measured again and again across related studies [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1], and the bank evidence there is photo-based case-study observation rather than measurement [ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2]. Every source in this row is from the USA, Canada or Europe, temperate and high-income; none reports a rainfed cropping system in a low- or lower-middle-income country. The European figures are model results from rich countries [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: For rainfed cropping the rating is the same as overall, a small reduction in erosion risk; eight papers name this farming system. Most of the large percentages below measure runoff and soil caught in the strip; the one estimate of soil loss avoided on the cropland itself is small. Below a rainfed row crop the buffer first takes the water out of the flow: switchgrass stops concentrated flow from the field and infiltration runs well above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], cutting runoff by 58.3% behind the 7 m grass buffer and 81.5% behind the wider grass-woody buffer over 19 natural precipitation events [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6] and by more than 77% in the Kansas plots [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. The sediment follows: 70% and more than 92% trapped under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% removed over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3] with a worst-case floor of 71% and 86% across all storms [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in the Kansas plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a corn strip was restored to fescue in Connecticut [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1], and fairly narrow strips of riparian vegetation reducing sediment input across the field studies reviewed [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15]. T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: Little of this row is a measured before-and-after of restoration. The Chinese strips were long-established rather than newly restored, and their numbers show the gap between vegetation types — 50% for shrubs against 92% for woody cover, over a bare control that already trapped 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]. The Costa Rican 3.9% is a model output, not a measurement, from a study whose authors say the sediment model over-estimates erosion on steep ground [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1]. The Brazilian values are correlations across a few watersheds [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], and several remaining findings are cited background, an uncited introductory assertion or farmer perception rather than measurement [ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11, ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5]. The McKergow finding is a citation within a review, not new measurement [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6], and the Brazilian trench study has no without-forest control: retention there is inferred from where buried sediment layers stop inside an existing forest, not measured against a cleared comparison [ev_sediment_retention_oliv10_1]. Width beyond the first stretch adds little [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], and nothing here reports how the strip performs in an extreme storm or once trapped sediment has accumulated. The mix is temperate high-income plus upper-middle-income China, Brazil and Mexico; no low-income measurement supports it.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: Where riparian vegetation is established or allowed to persist, sediment is intercepted before the channel and the bank is held. Trapping efficiency increases sharply over the first 10 m of buffer and then tails off [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], and fairly narrow strips of riparian vegetation reduce sediment input to surface water across the field studies reviewed [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1]. Measured along the Guishui River, outflow sediment fell by 92% under woody vegetation, 72% under grasses and 50% under shrubs, against a bare control trapping 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]. In Brazilian watersheds, suspended and organic solids decline as riparian forest cover rises [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], while bringing Costa Rican riparian forest to its legal minimum is modelled to raise sediment retention by 3.9% [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1]. McKergow et al. (2003) found that vegetation restoration of denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced catchment sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly by reducing bank erosion and stabilising the stream channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. In a Brazilian cotton field bordered by an existing native riparian forest, sediment eroded from the cropped slope formed layers up to 14 cm thick in trenches dug a few metres inside the forest, with no buried sediment layer found further in, where runoff had slowed enough for its sediment to settle out [ev_sediment_retention_oliv10_1]. On the bank, forested strips stabilise banks more effectively than grass [ev_streambank_erosion_osbo93_17], losing riparian forest to other land cover brings bank erosion [ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11], and farmers identify tree roots as what prevents riverbank erosion during floods [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5].

Switchgrass planted below the cropland stops concentrated flow and lets infiltration run above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], cutting runoff by 58.3% and 81.5% for the grass and the grass-woody buffer [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6] and by more than 77% in the Kansas plots [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. Sediment trapping follows the same pattern: 70% and more than 92% under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events with a floor of 71% and 86% across all storms [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 97% behind an 8 m fescue strip with 91% already achieved within 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped strip was seeded to fescue in Connecticut [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]; retained forest strips of 9 m sufficed to remove sediment from cutblock features and modelled widths below 60 m controlled sedimentation under most circumstances [ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1]. A US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass cover cut sediment concentration in overland flow by 92% [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_5]. Planting trees in the strip stabilises river banks, reducing erosion and sediment loss [ev_streambank_erosion_cole20_1]: willow posts trapped sediment and held further collapse to an additional 0.3 m of bank through the 1993 floods, and the poplar-planted reach kept its streambank integrity [ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2]. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they avoid 6.3% of the soil lost to water erosion on cropland in the landscapes where they are set up (1.2% across the EU and UK), and separately catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on European cropland [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: This practice reverses under conditions that are not rare, and the reversal is not confined to frozen or saturated extremes: riparian vegetation improves water quality through nitrogen uptake and denitrification, but in wet, oxygen-poor riparian soils, decomposing plant detritus can set up reducing conditions that desorb phosphate from iron complexes and pass dissolved phosphorus into the stream — the same vegetation-mediated processes working against the practice [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_2]. During most snowmelt runoff events the Guishui strips had little or no effect on nitrogen concentrations and runoff losses of total nitrogen, nitrate and ammonium increased at the buffer outlet — frozen ground turns the sink into a source [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_9]. During the dormant season both grass and forested Illinois strips released dissolved and total phosphorus to the groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_2]. Narrow buffers under 15 m actually contributed nitrogen to the riparian zone in six of the pooled studies [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_3], buffer outflow in the early stages of a natural runoff event can contribute pollutants to surface waters [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_5], and nutrient-saturated strips act as a source rather than a sink, with the highest risk during high flow, ice thaw and bank erosion [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_6]. In the Connecticut restoration, total Kjeldahl nitrogen and total phosphorus concentrations increased significantly as groundwater flowed through the restored buffer, and groundwater nitrogen species were otherwise unaffected [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_3, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_4]; part of the groundwater nitrate decline there was due to the cessation of fertilisation on the strip, not to the buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2]. Mass is not concentration: the Kansas buffers cut total phosphorus and total nitrogen mass by 91.8 and 92.1% but their concentrations by only 42.9 and 44.4% [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1], dissolved phosphorus concentration fell by just 16% [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_3] and nitrate by 10-19% against 48-72% for ammonium [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_4]. Storm intensity strips the effect away: removal fell to 50 and 28% for the grass buffer and 35% for phosphate behind the wider buffer at 69 mm per hour [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_6, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_7], phosphate mass was not significantly reduced at the higher intensity [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_8], and soluble removal held above 60% in every storm except the most intense [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8]. The width evidence contradicts itself — a meta-analysis found no impact of width on nitrogen removal efficiency and increasing width from 4 to 8 m did not reduce soluble herbicide loadings [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_3, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_1], while other work says wider is better with diminishing returns and that more than 200 m was needed for ideal efficiency in some cases [ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_4]. Time matters in both directions: nitrate reductions in the early stages of restoration may be much less than the figures reported for established buffers, which should not be extrapolated [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; and in one restored stream woody vegetation only established 13-17 years on, then shaded out the algal assimilation and ultimately contributed to increasing nutrient concentrations [ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_3]. In the fenced pasture buffer, the nutrient decline reversed after twelve years, once debris blockages became less common and aquatic macrophytes were shaded out by the now-established woody vegetation, and nutrient levels rose again — a long-term waning of the benefit, not a measured harm [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]. The catchment-scale sediment and the general nitrogen-removal findings above are themselves citations within a review, not new measurement [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_1, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_2, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_3, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]. The thermal benefit can invert as well: newly restored streams whose canopy was removed during construction had higher temperatures [ev_stream_temperature_mcmi14_1], and that study is urban restoration bundled with channel regrading, where the reach-scale nitrate result rests on a sample of three and the phosphate comparison was not significant [ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_2]. Context can remove the pathway entirely — buffers are not as effective where fields are tile drained, because the drains bypass them [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_6] — and cover type decides the outcome: a 20 m oat buffer had no significant effect on total phosphorus while a 10 m rye grass strip did [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_4, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5], the grass strip did little to reduce phosphorus in shallow groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_3], and across the reviewed studies no clear pattern was evident for subsurface phosphorus, with one study finding concentrations increased [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_14]. Finally, the largest percentages in the pool are modelled, not measured: the Costa Rican nitrogen and phosphorus retention gains of 81.4 and 85.9% fall to 35.1 and 37.1% under the study's own low retention-efficiency assumption [ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_1, ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_2], and the Guishui paper reports both 58% and 92.8% for phosphorus in the same treatment [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7]. The cooling evidence is from buffers left at harvest or from wooded strips in general; the only measurement on newly restored streams found that those with open canopy had higher temperatures [ev_stream_temperature_mcmi14_1], so cooling from a newly established strip is not shown here. Provenance is narrow: Illinois, Iowa, Kansas and Connecticut field sites — several of them repeat visits to the same Bear Creek reach — a pooled analysis that states no study country, and upper-middle-income work from China and Brazil; the Brazilian values are correlations whose authors stress that watershed-scale land cover explained water quality better than the riparian zone [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8]. No measurement here comes from a low-income farming system. The European figures are model results and the Quebec figures are cited second-hand; both come from rich countries [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: Three pathways carry this effect. Sediment-bound load settles out in the strip: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment trapped under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped riparian strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]; at catchment scale, McKergow et al. (2003) found that restoring vegetation to denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly through less bank erosion and a stabilised channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. Dissolved load is removed as water passes through and is taken up, mainly by plant uptake and by denitrification [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_1]: across 88 buffers in a pooled analysis, mean nitrogen removal effectiveness was 67.5%, at a rate of 0.394 mg per litre per metre of buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_2]; the Bear Creek buffers removed 80% and 94% of total nitrogen over 19 natural events [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4] and 64 to 72%, rising to 80 to 93% for the wider buffer, under a 25 mm per hour simulation [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5]; vadose-zone nitrate never exceeded 2 mg per litre inside the Iowa buffer while the adjacent field exceeded 12 [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2]; shallow groundwater nitrate fell by up to 90% behind Illinois buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_1], with reviewed ranges of 79-98% in surface runoff and 68-100% in groundwater for forested strips against 54-84% and 10-60% for grass [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_10, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_7, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9], and phosphorus reductions of 50-85% and 61-83% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_12, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5]; restoring a cropped strip cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen 70%, nitrate 83% and total phosphorus 73% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; a separately reviewed US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass showed a 35% reduction in groundwater nitrate [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_3]; in a long-term study of a trampled, overgrazed pasture riparian zone fenced off from livestock, rapid herbaceous and then woody regrowth was followed by declining stream nutrient levels over the first twelve years [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]; along the Guishui River an 18 m woody strip removed 89.8% of total nitrogen and 92.8% of total phosphorus, against 72.3% and 43.9% for grass and shrub strips and 17.62% with no buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_5, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_6, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_8]; and nutrients accumulate in standing biomass, 770 and 90 kg of nitrogen per hectare in Quebec poplar buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_1, ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1]. Third, shade: wooded strips moderate diel fluctuations in stream temperature [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1], buffers significantly reduced post-harvest temperature increases [ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3]. Correlational and modelled work points the same way [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_7, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1, ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_1]. Newer sources point the same way. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they would avoid about 33% of all nitrogen reaching water in the EU and UK, and catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on cropland [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6]. A Quebec cost study, citing earlier Quebec research second-hand, reports nitrate falling by 47 to 100% and soluble phosphorus by 22 to 89% after wooded strips were planted, and states that without streamside vegetation stream water can be 2 to 10°C warmer [ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].

justification.mechanism: Three pathways carry this effect. Sediment-bound load settles out in the strip: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment trapped under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped riparian strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]; at catchment scale, McKergow et al. (2003) found that restoring vegetation to denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly through less bank erosion and a stabilised channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. Dissolved load is removed as water passes through and is taken up, mainly by plant uptake and by denitrification [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_1]: across 88 buffers in a pooled analysis, mean nitrogen removal effectiveness was 67.5%, at a rate of 0.394 mg per litre per metre of buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_2]; the Bear Creek buffers removed 80% and 94% of total nitrogen over 19 natural events [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4] and 64 to 72%, rising to 80 to 93% for the wider buffer, under a 25 mm per hour simulation [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5]; vadose-zone nitrate never exceeded 2 mg per litre inside the Iowa buffer while the adjacent field exceeded 12 [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2]; shallow groundwater nitrate fell by up to 90% behind Illinois buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_1], with reviewed ranges of 79-98% in surface runoff and 68-100% in groundwater for forested strips against 54-84% and 10-60% for grass [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_10, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_7, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9], and phosphorus reductions of 50-85% and 61-83% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_12, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5]; restoring a cropped strip cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen 70%, nitrate 83% and total phosphorus 73% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; a separately reviewed US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass showed a 35% reduction in groundwater nitrate [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_3]; in a long-term study of a trampled, overgrazed pasture riparian zone fenced off from livestock, rapid herbaceous and then woody regrowth was followed by declining stream nutrient levels over the first twelve years [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]; along the Guishui River an 18 m woody strip removed 89.8% of total nitrogen and 92.8% of total phosphorus, against 72.3% and 43.9% for grass and shrub strips and 17.62% with no buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_5, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_6, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_8]; and nutrients accumulate in standing biomass, 770 and 90 kg of nitrogen per hectare in Quebec poplar buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_1, ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1]. Third, shade: wooded strips moderate diel fluctuations in stream temperature [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1], buffers significantly reduced post-harvest temperature increases [ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3]. Correlational and modelled work points the same way [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_7, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1, ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_1]. Newer sources point the same way. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they would avoid about 33% of all nitrogen reaching water in the EU and UK, and catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on cropland [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6]. A Quebec cost study, citing earlier Quebec research second-hand, reports nitrate falling by 47 to 100% and soluble phosphorus by 22 to 89% after wooded strips were planted, and states that without streamside vegetation stream water can be 2 to 10°C warmer [ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].

justification.statement: riparian_buffer strongly reduces water_quality_risk in BRA, CAN, CHN, CRI, GBR, USA; measured HARM (maladaptation) in 8 sources — the practice worsened this outcome for some adopters (robust evidence, high agreement → very_high confidence; transfer: out_of_context).

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: The same Chinese study carries the clearest failure mode in the corpus: during most snowmelt runoff events the strips had little or no effect on nitrogen concentrations and runoff losses of total nitrogen, nitrate and ammonium increased at the buffer outlet, the strip acting as a source [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_9]. It also disagrees with itself, reporting both 58% and 92.8% phosphorus removal for the same woody treatment on the same page [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7], and its shrub strips removed only 43.9% of nitrogen while the no-buffer control already removed 17.62% [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_6, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_8]; those buffers were long-established, not newly planted. The Brazilian figures are Pearson correlations across a handful of watersheds rather than measured removal, and their authors stress that land cover at the watershed scale explained water quality better than the riparian zone did [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4]. Much of the rest is cited background or uncited introductory assertion, including claims about buffers wider than 200 m and about forest buffers between urban areas and streams, which is not a rural pathway [ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_4, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12]. Nothing in this row reports performance under an extreme storm, or how the strip behaves once saturated with nutrients.
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: In the upper-middle-income evidence the strip intercepts both the particles and the dissolved load. Along the Guishui River an 18 m woody buffer removed 89.8% of total nitrogen and retained 92.8% of total phosphorus, where a grass strip reached 72.3% and a shrub strip only 43.9%, and in a 10 m strip woody vegetation cut total phosphorus by 69.3% against 17.62% with no buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_5, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_6, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_8]; the same strips cut outflow sediment by 92%, 72% and 50% for woody, grass and shrub cover against a bare control trapping 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]. In Brazilian third-order watersheds, in-stream nitrogen, phosphorus, suspended and organic solids and faecal coliforms all fall, and dissolved oxygen rises, as riparian-zone forest cover increases [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_7, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], which the authors read as grounds for prioritising riparian restoration as a short-term water-quality action [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1].

justification.statement: riparian_buffer strongly reduces water_quality_risk in BRA, CHN (upper_middle income contexts); measured HARM (maladaptation) in 1 source — the practice worsened this outcome for some adopters (medium evidence, high agreement → high confidence; transfer: in_context).

T6_nbs_scorecard.conditionality: The failure modes are seasonal, hydrological and chemical. During the dormant season both the grass and the forested strip released dissolved and total phosphorus to the groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_2], and buffer outflow in the early stages of a natural runoff event can itself contribute pollutants to surface waters [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_5]. In the Connecticut restoration, total Kjeldahl nitrogen and total phosphorus increased significantly as groundwater flowed through the restored buffer, while groundwater nitrogen species were otherwise not significantly influenced [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_3, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_4]; part of the 35% groundwater nitrate decline there came from stopping fertilisation rather than from the buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2], and the authors warn that nitrate reductions in the early stages of restoration may be much less than the figures reported for established buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]. Mass is not concentration: the Kansas mass reductions of 91.8 and 92.1% correspond to concentration reductions of only 42.9 and 44.4%, dissolved phosphorus fell by just 16%, and nitrate by 10-19% against 48-72% for ammonium [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_4]. Intensity breaks the soluble fraction: at 69 mm per hour removal fell to 50 and 28% for the grass buffer and 35% for phosphate behind the wider buffer, phosphate mass was not significantly reduced at that intensity, and soluble removal stayed above 60% in every storm but the most intense [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_6, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_7, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8]. Buffers are not as effective where fields are tile drained, because the drains bypass them [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_6] — a direct limit on this farming system — and the cover planted decides the result: a 20 m oat buffer had no significant effect on total phosphorus where a 10 m rye grass strip did [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_4, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5], the grass strip did little for phosphorus in shallow groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_3], and across the reviewed studies no clear pattern was evident for subsurface phosphorus, with one study finding it increased [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_14]. Clay is the fraction least trapped, at 52% against 93% for sand and silt [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3], and the Prince Edward Island widening figures are model output whose added retention from 50 m to 100 m is only 4.6 and 4.0% [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2]. Provenance is narrow even within rainfed cropping: Iowa, Illinois, Kansas, Connecticut and Prince Edward Island, with the Bear Creek reach measured repeatedly across related studies [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1], all temperate and high-income, and much of the Illinois material cited from other reviews rather than measured on site. The European figures are model results and the Quebec figures are cited second-hand; both come from rich countries [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].
T6_nbs_scorecard.effect_mechanism: For rainfed cropping the rating is the same as overall, a strong reduction in water-quality risk; nine papers name this farming system. Below rainfed row crops the strip removes what the runoff carries and what the shallow groundwater brings. Over 19 natural events at Bear Creek, the grass buffer removed 95% of sediment, 80% of total nitrogen, 62% of nitrate and 58% of phosphate, and the wider grass-woody buffer 97%, 94%, 85% and 80% [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9]; under simulated rainfall the same design removed 64 to 72% and 80 to 93% of incoming nutrients [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3]. Vadose-zone nitrate inside the Iowa buffer never exceeded 2 mg per litre while the adjacent fields exceeded 12 [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]. Restoring a cropped Connecticut strip to fescue cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen by 70%, nitrate by 83%, total phosphorus by 73% and suspended solids by 92%, and groundwater nitrate by 35% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2, ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]. On the Illinois floodplain, both the forested and the grass strip reduced shallow-groundwater nitrate by up to 90% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_1], with reviewed reductions of 79-98% and 54-84% in surface runoff, 68-100% and 40-100% in groundwater for forested strips against 10-60% for grass, and phosphorus reductions of 50-85% and 61-83% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_10, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_7, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_12, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5]; the Kansas grass-shrub plots cut suspended-solids mass by 99.7% and total phosphorus and nitrogen mass by about 92% [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1], and sediment-bound load is intercepted by even fairly narrow strips [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Newer sources point the same way. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they would avoid about 33% of all nitrogen reaching water in the EU and UK, and catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on cropland [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6]. A Quebec cost study, citing earlier Quebec research second-hand, reports nitrate falling by 47 to 100% and soluble phosphorus by 22 to 89% after wooded strips were planted, and states that without streamside vegetation stream water can be 2 to 10°C warmer [ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].

justification.conditionality: The failure modes are seasonal, hydrological and chemical. During the dormant season both the grass and the forested strip released dissolved and total phosphorus to the groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_2], and buffer outflow in the early stages of a natural runoff event can itself contribute pollutants to surface waters [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_5]. In the Connecticut restoration, total Kjeldahl nitrogen and total phosphorus increased significantly as groundwater flowed through the restored buffer, while groundwater nitrogen species were otherwise not significantly influenced [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_3, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_4]; part of the 35% groundwater nitrate decline there came from stopping fertilisation rather than from the buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2], and the authors warn that nitrate reductions in the early stages of restoration may be much less than the figures reported for established buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]. Mass is not concentration: the Kansas mass reductions of 91.8 and 92.1% correspond to concentration reductions of only 42.9 and 44.4%, dissolved phosphorus fell by just 16%, and nitrate by 10-19% against 48-72% for ammonium [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_4]. Intensity breaks the soluble fraction: at 69 mm per hour removal fell to 50 and 28% for the grass buffer and 35% for phosphate behind the wider buffer, phosphate mass was not significantly reduced at that intensity, and soluble removal stayed above 60% in every storm but the most intense [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_6, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_7, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8]. Buffers are not as effective where fields are tile drained, because the drains bypass them [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_6] — a direct limit on this farming system — and the cover planted decides the result: a 20 m oat buffer had no significant effect on total phosphorus where a 10 m rye grass strip did [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_4, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5], the grass strip did little for phosphorus in shallow groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_3], and across the reviewed studies no clear pattern was evident for subsurface phosphorus, with one study finding it increased [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_14]. Clay is the fraction least trapped, at 52% against 93% for sand and silt [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3], and the Prince Edward Island widening figures are model output whose added retention from 50 m to 100 m is only 4.6 and 4.0% [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2]. Provenance is narrow even within rainfed cropping: Iowa, Illinois, Kansas, Connecticut and Prince Edward Island, with the Bear Creek reach measured repeatedly across related studies [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1], all temperate and high-income, and much of the Illinois material cited from other reviews rather than measured on site. The European figures are model results and the Quebec figures are cited second-hand; both come from rich countries [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].

justification.mechanism: For rainfed cropping the rating is the same as overall, a strong reduction in water-quality risk; nine papers name this farming system. Below rainfed row crops the strip removes what the runoff carries and what the shallow groundwater brings. Over 19 natural events at Bear Creek, the grass buffer removed 95% of sediment, 80% of total nitrogen, 62% of nitrate and 58% of phosphate, and the wider grass-woody buffer 97%, 94%, 85% and 80% [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9]; under simulated rainfall the same design removed 64 to 72% and 80 to 93% of incoming nutrients [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3]. Vadose-zone nitrate inside the Iowa buffer never exceeded 2 mg per litre while the adjacent fields exceeded 12 [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]. Restoring a cropped Connecticut strip to fescue cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen by 70%, nitrate by 83%, total phosphorus by 73% and suspended solids by 92%, and groundwater nitrate by 35% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2, ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]. On the Illinois floodplain, both the forested and the grass strip reduced shallow-groundwater nitrate by up to 90% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_1], with reviewed reductions of 79-98% and 54-84% in surface runoff, 68-100% and 40-100% in groundwater for forested strips against 10-60% for grass, and phosphorus reductions of 50-85% and 61-83% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_10, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_7, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_12, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5]; the Kansas grass-shrub plots cut suspended-solids mass by 99.7% and total phosphorus and nitrogen mass by about 92% [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1], and sediment-bound load is intercepted by even fairly narrow strips [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Newer sources point the same way. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they would avoid about 33% of all nitrogen reaching water in the EU and UK, and catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on cropland [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6]. A Quebec cost study, citing earlier Quebec research second-hand, reports nitrate falling by 47 to 100% and soluble phosphorus by 22 to 89% after wooded strips were planted, and states that without streamside vegetation stream water can be 2 to 10°C warmer [ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].
